card.name: Verbs and word-ends in interaction warnings
card.fires_on: Words that come right after a drug, enzyme or clotting-factor name in warnings, such as 'may' or 'have', and the middle or end of names like antithrombin, C-1 esterase and CYP2D6.

modes.label: Verb after a drug subject
modes.description: 'may' or 'have' follows a drug or metabolizer group and leads into an effect statement.
modes.example: which<< may>> increase the risk of BCRP substrate

modes.label: Inside lab or enzyme names
modes.description: Part of a name for a clotting factor or enzyme, such as antithrombin, C-1 esterase or CYP2D6.
modes.example: Antithrom<<bin>> deficiency or Protein C or S deficiency

card.plain: It marks the point in an interaction or risk warning where a drug name leads into the effect, or where an enzyme or clotting-factor name is partly written.
